mainTopic: The status of a בן פקוע (a live fetus found in its slaughtered mother): whether it needs its own שחיטה, and whether the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי that it never does.
overview: The amud opens with רב חסדא's ruling: a live nine-month fetus found in a slaughtered animal needs its own שחיטה, yet if it dies it is not a נבלה. רבא objects that this mixes רבי מאיר and the רבנן. רב חסדא first points to a ברייתא of רבי חייא, and רבא rejects that support. רב חסדא then answers that the תורה made four סימנים valid for the fetus, so his whole ruling fits the רבנן. רב אסי reports that רבי יוחנן said the same, though no one knows whether ריש לקיש agreed. The גמרא then turns to רבי שמעון שזורי in the משנה. He and the תנא קמא differ over a בן פקוע that walked on the ground. Several rulings follow about a בן פקוע's offspring and about uncloven animals, and זעירי rules like רבי שמעון שזורי. In a real case, רב אשי tells אדא בר חבו to slaughter his injured בן פקוע, because he follows רבי יונתן: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי only for a מסוכן and for תרומת מעשר of דמאי, whose source משניות the גמרא then quotes.

steps.title: The live fetus needs its own slaughter but stays pure if it dies
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא finishes his ruling. The live fetus needs שחיטה and the כהן's gifts, but if it dies it does not make people impure by carrying it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It needs slaughter, and the owner must give the foreleg, jaw, and maw to a כהן. But if it dies, it does not make someone impure through carrying it.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of רב חסדא's ruling about a live nine-month fetus found inside a slaughtered animal. He tells us how we treat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling has two halves. First, the fetus is treated like its own animal: it needs its own שחיטה, and the gifts to the כהן apply to it. Second, if it dies before being slaughtered, it is still pure and does not count as a נבלה. That second half quietly assumes the mother's שחיטה still 'covers' it.

keyTerms.meaning: Requires (its own) ritual slaughter
Foreleg, jaw, and maw: the gifts given to a כהן from a slaughtered non-sacred animal
Pure in the sense that it does not make a person impure by carrying it (that is, it is not a נבלה)

phrases.english: It requires slaughter,
phrases.notes: We are in the middle of רב חסדא's ruling. 'It' is a live nine-month fetus found inside an animal that was slaughtered.

phrases.english: and it is obligated in the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw,
but if it dies,
it is pure with regard to imparting impurity through carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָעוּן שְׁחִיטָה, וְחַיָּיב בִּזְרוֹעַ וְהַלְּחָיַיִם וְהַקֵּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב חסדא's ruling, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A live nine-month fetus needs its own שחיטה and is subject to the כהן's gifts. If it dies, it does not impart נבלה impurity.

steps.title: רבא: your ruling mixes two opposing opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the first half of the ruling follows רבי מאיר and the second half follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: 'It needs slaughter' follows whom? רבי מאיר. 'If it dies it is pure from carrying' follows whom? The רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב חסדא. He says the ruling is inconsistent because each half matches a different side of a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר holds that a live nine-month fetus is its own animal and needs its own שחיטה. On that view, if it dies, it should be a נבלה. The רבנן hold that the mother's שחיטה covers it. On that view, it stays pure. You cannot say 'needs שחיטה' like רבי מאיר and also 'pure after death' like the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Which sage's opinion does this follow?
The Sages, the majority view that argues with רבי מאיר

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying either half is wrong by itself. His problem is combining the two halves into one ruling.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
"It requires slaughter": in accordance with whom?
In accordance with Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם מֵת טָהוֹר מִלְּטַמֵּא בְּמַשָּׂא – כְּמַאן?
phrases.english: and "if it dies it is pure with regard to imparting impurity through carrying": in accordance with whom?
In accordance with the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: טָעוּן שְׁחִיטָה – כְּמַאן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 1 as internally inconsistent.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's two-part ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Requiring שחיטה means the fetus is its own animal (רבי מאיר). If so, it should be a נבלה when it dies. Saying it stays pure follows the רבנן, so the ruling contradicts itself.

steps.title: רב חסדא: רבי חייא's ברייתא says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא defends himself. A ברייתא of רבי חייא has the exact same two-part ruling, so רבא's question would hit it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, what about the ברייתא of רבי חייא? One who slaughters a טרפה and finds a live nine-month fetus inside: it needs slaughter, the כהן's gifts apply, and if it dies it is pure from carrying. That 'needs slaughter' would follow רבי מאיר, and 'pure if it dies' would follow the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers by pointing to a ברייתא that rules exactly as he did. If רבא's objection were valid, it would apply to the ברייתא too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a 'ולטעמיך' move: it turns the challenge back on the challenger. רב חסדא's point is that a recognized ברייתא already combines these two halves. So the combination must be acceptable, and his ruling has support.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: a reply showing the challenger's logic would cause trouble elsewhere
An animal with a fatal defect, which is forbidden to eat even after שחיטה
A live, fully developed (nine-month) fetus

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
what about that which Rabbi Chiyya teaches:
One who slaughters a tereifa
and found inside it a live nine-month-old fetus,

phrases.aramaic: טָעוּן שְׁחִיטָה, וְחַיָּיב בִּזְרוֹעַ וְהַלְּחָיַיִם וְהַקֵּבָה,
phrases.english: it requires slaughter, and it is obligated in the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw,
but if it dies, it is pure with regard to imparting impurity through carrying.
"It requires slaughter": in accordance with whom? Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם מֵת – טָהוֹר מִלְּטַמֵּא בְּמַשָּׂא, כְּרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: and "if it dies it is pure with regard to imparting impurity through carrying": in accordance with the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, הָא דְתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 1 against step 2 by showing a ברייתא with the identical ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That combining 'needs שחיטה' with 'pure after death' is a legitimate ruling.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא about a fetus found inside a slaughtered טרפה.

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא means a fetus already found dead
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof. רבי חייא's 'if it dies' means it was already dead inside the mother, a case where even רבי מאיר agrees it is pure. רב חסדא's ruling is still difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is no problem: רבי חייא is talking about where it was already found dead. But for you, it is still a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back the proof from the ברייתא. He reads it differently, and that leaves רב חסדא's ruling without support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the ברייתא's 'if it dies' as 'if it was found already dead inside the mother.' Everyone agrees, רבי מאיר included, that the mother's שחיטה makes such a fetus pure. So the whole ברייתא fits רבי מאיר. רב חסדא, however, was talking about a fetus born alive that died later, and there his ruling still mixes opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not difficult: the challenge from this source is dismissed
He already found it dead (inside the mother)
For you it is difficult: the original problem remains against you

steps.whatToRemember: A fetus found alive that later dies is the case where רבי מאיר and the רבנן disagree. A fetus already found dead inside its slaughtered mother is pure according to everyone. רבא uses this difference to keep his challenge against רב חסדא standing.

phrases.english: That is not difficult,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא אִם כְּבָר מְצָאוֹ מֵת קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya is speaking about where he already found it dead,
but according to you, it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, רַבִּי חִיָּיא אִם כְּבָר מְצָאוֹ מֵת קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3 and reasserts the challenge of step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of רבי חייא's ברייתא as support for רב חסדא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא speaks of a fetus already found dead, where all agree it is pure. רב חסדא speaks of a fetus found alive that died later, which is a different case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא fits רבי מאיר alone, while רב חסדא's ruling still appears to mix רבי מאיר and the רבנן.

steps.title: רב חסדא: Four סימנים Make the Fetus Fit
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says his ruling is not split between two opinions. It follows the רבנן completely, because the תורה made four סימנים valid for the fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רבא: Even according to my own reading there is no difficulty. The Merciful One made four סימנים valid for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers רבא's challenge from Step 2. He shows that his whole ruling can follow one opinion, the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the first half of the ruling (it needs שחיטה) sounds like רבי מאיר. רב חסדא answers that even for the רבנן, the fetus can be made permitted in two ways: by its mother's two סימנים or by its own two. Since the mother's שחיטה already counts for it, it is pure if it dies, and its own שחיטה is also valid, so both halves fit the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: According to me / my own view
It is not difficult; there is no problem
Four סימנים: the windpipe and food pipe of the mother plus those of the fetus
The Merciful One (the תורה) made it valid

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's key idea: the fetus has four valid סימנים, so either its mother's שחיטה or its own permits it.

phrases.english: He said to him:
According to me too, it is not difficult,
phrases.notes: He means: even my own reading, where the whole ruling follows the רבנן, has no problem.

phrases.english: four simanim
phrases.notes: The two of the mother and the two of the fetus.

phrases.english: the Merciful One made valid for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִידִי נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא rejected the proof from רבי חייא, רב חסדא gives a new answer of his own.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the whole ruling follows one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed split: needing שחיטה like רבי מאיר, and being pure after death like the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both halves fit the רבנן, because the fetus has four valid סימנים.

steps.title: רב אסי Confirms: רבי יוחנן Says the Same
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל, רב אסי hears רבי זירא saying רב חסדא's teaching. He tells him it is correct, and that רבי יוחנן said the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא went up to ארץ ישראל, רב אסי found him sitting and saying this teaching. He said to him: Well said, and so said רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that backs up רב חסדא's 'four סימנים' teaching. A great sage in ארץ ישראל, רבי יוחנן, held the same view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is support, not a new argument. רב חסדא's idea from בבל matches what רבי יוחנן taught in ארץ ישראל, which makes it stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up, meaning moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל
A teaching or ruling
Well said! That is correct

phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira went up,
phrases.notes: He went up from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Rav Asi found him
sitting and saying it,
this teaching.
phrases.notes: The 'four סימנים' teaching of רב חסדא.

phrases.english: He said to him: Well said,
and so said Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִישַׁר, וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 5 with the same view from רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement, reported by רב אסי

steps.title: Did ריש לקיש Disagree?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether mentioning רבי יוחנן means that ריש לקיש, his usual partner in debate, disagreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we infer from this that רבי שמעון בן לקיש disagrees with him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks a clarifying question. Why name only רבי יוחנן? Was ריש לקיש against it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש often argue. Saying 'so said רבי יוחנן' with no mention of ריש לקיש could hint that ריש לקיש held the other view.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; it follows that
Disagrees

phrases.english: Is it inferred that he disagrees with him,
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what follows from naming רבי יוחנן alone in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ריש לקיש disagreed with the 'four סימנים' view

steps.title: ריש לקיש Stayed Silent
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי answers that ריש לקיש said nothing. Either he was waiting to see if רבי יוחנן would take it back, or, some say, he was busy drinking. So his view is unknown.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was waiting for him and kept silent. And some say: he was drinking and kept silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי answers רבי זירא's question. He cannot say whether ריש לקיש disagreed, because ריש לקיש did not speak up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of why ריש לקיש was quiet. In one, he waited to see if רבי יוחנן would change his mind. In the other, he was drinking. Either way, his silence does not prove he agreed, and the question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: Waited
Was silent
Was drinking

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up שָׁתֵי (drinking) and שָׁתֵיק (silent). The two words sound alike, and that sound-alike is what the second version plays on.

phrases.english: He was waiting for him
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש was waiting to see if רבי יוחנן would take back what he said.

phrases.english: and kept silent,
and some say:
he was busy drinking
and kept silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְׁהָא הֲוָה שָׁהֵי לֵיהּ וְשָׁתֵיק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Unknown. ריש לקיש was silent, either waiting or drinking, so we cannot tell if he disagreed.

steps.title: רבי שמעון שזורי Seems Identical to the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes רבי שמעון שזורי. It asks why he is listed separately, since he seems to say the same thing as the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון שזורי says: Even, etc. That is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. It then challenges it: the two opinions look identical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא already said a fetus found alive in its slaughtered mother does not need שחיטה. רבי שמעון שזורי says 'even' if it grew up and plows the field. If they agree, why does the משנה record a separate opinion?

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
That is the same as
Etc.; the rest of the quote

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
Even, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה: even if it is five years old and plowing in the field, it needs no שחיטה.

phrases.english: That is the same as the first tanna!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב חסדא discussion and returns to the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The separate opinion of רבי שמעון שזורי in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If his view matches the תנא קמא, there is no reason to list it separately.

steps.title: The Difference: A Fetus That Walked on the Ground
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that the two disagree about a fetus that has walked on the ground. The תנא קמא requires שחיטה because of a rabbinic decree, and רבי שמעון שזורי does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The difference between them is a case where it stood on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the challenge by showing a real case where the two opinions give different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, once the fetus walks on the ground the חכמים require שחיטה. Otherwise people seeing it might think other animals can be eaten without שחיטה. רבי שמעון שזורי does not make this decree, so he says it needs no שחיטה even then.

keyTerms.meaning: Stood with its hooves on the ground, meaning it walked around
There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: The two opinions differ over a fetus that walked on the ground. The תנא קמא requires שחיטה by rabbinic decree, and רבי שמעון שזורי never requires it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the core rule is the same for both, since the תורה permits the fetus through its mother. They argue only about a rabbinic safeguard.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
it stood with its hooves on the ground
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִפְרִיס עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a practical difference between the opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא and רבי שמעון שזורי say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ over a fetus that walked on the ground: the תנא קמא requires שחיטה by rabbinic decree, and רבי שמעון שזורי does not.

steps.title: The offspring of a בן פקוע and a regular animal has no fix
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא says that according to the view that the father's lineage counts, the offspring of a בן פקוע father and a regular mother can never be made permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: According to the one who says we must take the father's lineage into account, if a בן פקוע mated with a regular animal, the baby has no way to be fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא brings a new problem case: a בן פקוע father and a regular mother. According to one view, their baby can never become permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father counts, the baby is half like its father, which needs no שחיטה, and half like its mother, which needs שחיטה. One baby cannot be both, so no act of שחיטה can properly permit it. The ruling depends on the view that the father's lineage counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus found alive inside its mother after she was slaughtered. It is permitted through its mother's שחיטה.
We take the father's lineage into account when setting the animal's status.
A regular, full animal that is not a בן פקוע.
It has no fix, meaning there is no way to make it permitted.

steps.confusionAlert: This is only according to the view that the father counts. According to the view that only the mother counts, this baby simply follows its regular mother and needs normal שחיטה.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
According to the one who says we must take the father's lineage into account,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן פְּקוּעָה הַבָּא עַל בְּהֵמָה מְעַלַּיְיתָא –
phrases.english: if a ben pekua mated with a regular animal,
phrases.notes: The בן פקוע here is the father, and the mother is an ordinary animal.

phrases.english: the baby has no way to be fixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: לְדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְזֶרַע הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון שזורי, the גמרא now looks at a special case: the offspring of a בן פקוע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the view that the father counts, the offspring of a בן פקוע father and a regular mother can never be permitted, even by שחיטה.

steps.title: Everyone permits a בן פקוע with uncloven hooves
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that even the תנא קמא agrees that a בן פקוע with uncloven hooves is permitted, because people remember strange things and will not confuse it with a normal animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees that a בן פקוע with uncloven hooves is permitted. Why? People always remember anything strange.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a case where even the תנא קמא agrees with רבי שמעון שזורי. A בן פקוע with uncloven hooves is permitted without שחיטה, even after it walks on the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא required שחיטה only because of a rabbinic decree. The worry was that people would see a normal-looking animal eaten without שחיטה and copy that with ordinary animals. An animal with odd, uncloven hooves is so strange that people will remember it, so there is no reason for the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose hooves are not split, which is unusual for a kosher animal.
Everyone agrees, meaning even the side that usually argues.
A strange or surprising thing.
They certainly remember.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the decree of the תנא קמא depends on how likely people are to get confused. When there is no chance of confusion, the decree does not apply.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּקָלוּט בֶּן פְּקוּעָה שֶׁמּוּתָּר,
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that a ben pekua with uncloven hooves is permitted,
What is the reason?
Any strange thing
people definitely remember it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּקָלוּט בֶּן פְּקוּעָה שֶׁמּוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב כהנא's explanation in step 10 that the תנא קמא's requirement is only a rabbinic decree, and shows when that decree does not apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן פקוע with uncloven hooves is permitted by everyone, since its strangeness keeps people from confusing it with a normal animal.

steps.title: Another version: אביי needs two strange features
steps.stepSummary: Some report that אביי gave a narrower case: the uncloven בן פקוע must be found inside an uncloven mother that was itself born to a kosher animal. Two strange features are needed before people will remember.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say אביי said: Everyone agrees that an uncloven animal, born to an uncloven mother, which is a בן פקוע, is permitted. Why? People definitely remember two strange things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of אביי's statement. In this version the case is narrower and needs two strange features, not just one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, one strange feature (uncloven hooves) was enough to remove the worry. In this version, one strange thing might not stand out enough. Only when the animal and its mother are both uncloven are people sure to remember.

keyTerms.meaning: Born to a mother whose hooves are not split.
Two strange things.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new sage arguing. It is the same אביי, reported in a different way, and the only change is how strict the case is.

phrases.english: Some say: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּקָלוּט בֶּן קְלוּטָה בֶּן פְּקוּעָה
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that an uncloven animal, born to an uncloven mother, which is a ben pekua,
is permitted.
What is the reason?
People definitely remember two strange things.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, narrower version of אביי's statement in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only with two strange features (uncloven animal from an uncloven mother) does everyone agree the בן פקוע is permitted.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי for all generations
steps.stepSummary: זעירי, quoting רבי חנינא, rules like רבי שמעון שזורי and adds that רבי שמעון שזורי permitted the בן פקוע's offspring forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said in the name of רבי חנינא: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי. Also, רבי שמעון שזורי used to permit its child and its grandchild, until the end of all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives a ruling: the הלכה is like רבי שמעון שזורי, so a בן פקוע needs no שחיטה even after walking on the ground. It also adds that he extended this to all its descendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי, quoting רבי חנינא, rules on the מחלוקת from step 10 in favor of רבי שמעון שזורי. He also adds that this leniency covers the בן פקוע's children and grandchildren forever, not just the בן פקוע itself. Later, in steps 18-20, רב אשי does not accept this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion.
Its child and its grandchild.
Until the end of all generations, meaning forever.
Permits.

steps.whyThisMatters: The story of אדא בר חבו that follows turns on this ruling. אדא quotes it against רב אשי, and רב אשי ends up not following it.

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי מַתִּיר
phrases.english: and likewise Rabbi Shimon Shezuri used to permit
its child and its grandchild,
until the end of all generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר זְעֵירִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון שזורי from steps 9 and 10 and decides the הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי: a בן פקוע and all its descendants are permitted without שחיטה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the בן פקוע is permitted, its child is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the leniency: the בן פקוע itself is permitted, but its offspring needs שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is permitted, but its child is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different view about the descendants. He agrees the בן פקוע itself is permitted without שחיטה, but its offspring is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a plain reading, רבי יוחנן does not argue about the בן פקוע itself. He only disagrees with stretching the leniency to the next generation. In step 18, however, רב אשי reads him as only describing רבי שמעון שזורי's view, not giving his own ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: It itself, the בן פקוע, is permitted without שחיטה.
But its child is forbidden unless it is slaughtered.

steps.whatToRemember: זעירי permits the בן פקוע and all its descendants. רבי יוחנן seems to permit the בן פקוע itself but forbid its child without שחיטה. In step 18, רב אשי reads רבי יוחנן as only describing רבי שמעון שזורי's view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is permitted, but its child is forbidden.
phrases.notes: "It" is the בן פקוע itself, and "forbidden" means forbidden unless it is slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הוּא מוּתָּר, וּבְנוֹ אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the second half of step 14, the part about descendants, but not the first half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בן פקוע itself needs no שחיטה, but its offspring does.

steps.title: A real case: רב אשי says to slaughter the injured בן פקוע
steps.stepSummary: אדא בר חבו's בן פקוע was attacked by a bear, and רב אשי tells him to go slaughter it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אדא בר חבו had a בן פקוע that a bear attacked. He came before רב אשי. רב אשי told him: Go slaughter it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real story about an injured בן פקוע. רב אשי rules that it should be slaughtered, and this sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal was about to die, so the owner wanted to know how to save the meat. Telling him to do שחיטה matches the תנא קמא, who requires שחיטה once a בן פקוע has walked on the ground. That seems to go against the ruling in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: A bear (here, a bear attacked the animal).
Go slaughter it.
He came before him to ask a question of הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: אַדָּא בַּר חָבוּ הֲוָה לֵיהּ בֶּן פְּקוּעָה
phrases.english: Adda bar Chavu had a ben pekua
that a bear attacked,
He came before Rav Ashi.
He said to him: Go slaughter it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדָּא בַּר חָבוּ הֲוָה לֵיהּ בֶּן פְּקוּעָה דִּנְפַל דֵּיבָא עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that tests the ruling from steps 14 and 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי instructs that the injured בן פקוע be slaughtered.

steps.title: אדא challenges רב אשי using זעירי and רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: אדא בר חבו objects: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי, and even רבי יוחנן only argued about the offspring, not the בן פקוע itself. So why does it need שחיטה?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But זעירי said in the name of רבי חנינא that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי, and that רבי שמעון שזורי permitted its child and grandchild until the end of all generations. And even רבי יוחנן only spoke about its child, not about the animal itself!
steps.whatsHappening: אדא challenges רב אשי's ruling. He quotes the ruling from steps 14 and 15 to show that his animal should be permitted without שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree the בן פקוע itself needs no שחיטה. זעירי permits everything, and רבי יוחנן argued only about the child. So רב אשי's instruction to slaughter seems to go against every view that was quoted. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? This opens a challenge from an earlier statement.
He only said; it limits what someone's statement covers.
It itself (here, the בן פקוע itself).

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now אדא בר חבו is speaking to רב אשי.

phrases.english: But didn't Ze'eiri say in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי מַתִּיר
phrases.english: and likewise Rabbi Shimon Shezuri used to permit

phrases.aramaic: בִּבְנוֹ וּבֶן בְּנוֹ עַד סוֹף כׇּל הַדּוֹרוֹת,
phrases.english: its child and its grandchild until the end of all generations,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא קָאָמַר אֶלָּא בְּנוֹ,
phrases.english: and even Rabbi Yochanan only spoke about its child,
but not about it itself!
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן also permits the בן פקוע itself, which is exactly what this animal is.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָאָמַר זְעֵירִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's ruling in step 16 using the rulings from steps 14 and 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's instruction to slaughter the בן פקוע (step 16).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי, and even רבי יוחנן agrees the בן פקוע itself is permitted. So requiring שחיטה goes against every quoted view.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was only explaining רבי שמעון שזורי's view
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that רבי יוחנן was not ruling like רבי שמעון שזורי. He was only describing how far רבי שמעון שזורי's leniency goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: רבי יוחנן was speaking according to the view of רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers אדא בר חבו's question. רבי יוחנן's statement was only explaining what רבי שמעון שזורי holds, not giving the final הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדא בר חבו thought that רבי יוחנן agreed the בן פקוע itself is permitted without שחיטה. רב אשי rereads רבי יוחנן's words: he only said that even רבי שמעון שזורי permits just the בן פקוע and not its offspring. רבי יוחנן himself may still hold like the תנא קמא, that the בן פקוע needs שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of. You are explaining someone else's opinion, not necessarily your own.
A calf found alive inside its mother after the mother was slaughtered.
Kosher ritual slaughter.
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי יוחנן as ruling that a בן פקוע is permitted. According to רב אשי, he was only describing the limits of רבי שמעון שזורי's leniency.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב אשי is answering אדא בר חבו.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי קָאָמַר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan was speaking according to the words of Rabbi Shimon Shezuri.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 17 by rereading רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of an אמורא's statement: he was explaining someone else's view, not ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן ruled that the בן פקוע itself is permitted without שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן only described the limits of רבי שמעון שזורי's view. The final הלכה can still require שחיטה.

steps.title: But the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי everywhere in our משנה
steps.stepSummary: אדא בר חבו objects using a tradition from רבי חנינא: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי in every place he taught in our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבין בר חנינא said, quoting עולא, quoting רבי חנינא: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי. And not only that, but every place רבי שמעון שזורי taught in our משנה, the הלכה follows him!
steps.whatsHappening: אדא בר חבו pushes back. Even if רבי יוחנן only explained a view, there is a general rule that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי everywhere in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 removed רבי יוחנן as support for the leniency. Now אדא בר חבו brings a broader rule: wherever רבי שמעון שזורי appears in our משנה, we rule like him. That would include his leniency about the בן פקוע, so the בן פקוע should not need שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say? Introduces a challenge from another statement.
The practical law follows [this sage].
And not only that, but... Introduces a wider claim.
Our משנה, meaning the official collection of משניות.

phrases.english: But didn't Ravin bar Chanina say
that Ulla said that Rabbi Chanina said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri,
and not only that, but

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי בְּמִשְׁנָתֵנוּ –
phrases.english: in every place that Rabbi Shimon Shezuri taught in our Mishnah,
the halacha follows him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רָבִין בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer in step 18 by bringing a general rule of הלכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's ruling that the בן פקוע needs שחיטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי everywhere in our משנה, it also follows his leniency about the בן פקוע. Then no שחיטה is needed.

steps.title: רב אשי follows רבי יונתן, who limits the rule to two cases
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says he holds like רבי יונתן. The הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי only for a מסוכן and for תרומת מעשר of דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I hold like this, as רבי יונתן said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי in the case of a dangerously ill person, and in the case of תרומת מעשר of דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that he does not accept the 'everywhere' rule. He follows רבי יונתן, who says we rule like רבי שמעון שזורי in only two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two traditions about how widely we follow רבי שמעון שזורי. רב אשי picks the narrow one: only the מסוכן case and the תרומת מעשר of דמאי case. The בן פקוע is not one of them, so there we follow the תנא קמא, and the animal needs שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: I hold like this [other opinion].
A person who is dangerously ill.
The portion the לוי must give to a כהן from the מעשר he receives.
Produce bought from someone who may not have tithed it, so it is doubtfully tithed.

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי rules that a בן פקוע needs שחיטה. The rule 'הלכה כרבי שמעון שזורי' applies only to a מסוכן and to תרומת מעשר of דמאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the story of אדא בר חבו: his בן פקוע must be slaughtered, because the בן פקוע case is not one of the two cases where we follow רבי שמעון שזורי.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא כִּי הָא סְבִירָא לִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: I hold in accordance with this,
as Rabbi Yonatan said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri in the case of a dangerously ill person,
and in the case of terumat ma'aser of demai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא כִּי הָא סְבִירָא לִי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by choosing a narrower tradition about when we rule like רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Competing tradition: he relies on a different אמורא who limits the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי everywhere in the משנה, including the בן פקוע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה follows him only for a מסוכן and for תרומת מעשר of דמאי, so a בן פקוע needs שחיטה.

steps.title: Where the dangerously ill case comes from: the divorce משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in גיטין where רבי שמעון שזורי extends the rule of 'write a גט for my wife' to a person who is dangerously ill.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מסוכן case is as we learned in a משנה: At first they used to say, if a man is being led out in a neck chain to be executed and says, 'Write a גט for my wife,' the people who hear him should write it and give it to her. Later they said: the same is true even of someone setting sail or leaving with a caravan. רבי שמעון בן שזורי says: even someone who is dangerously ill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the first of רבי יונתן's two cases. It quotes the משנה where רבי שמעון שזורי rules about a מסוכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a man must clearly tell people to write and give a גט. The משנה says that in certain dangerous situations, 'write a גט' alone is enough, and we assume he also meant 'give it.' The cases grow step by step: first a man going to execution, then travelers by sea or caravan, and רבי שמעון שזורי adds a man who is dangerously ill. This is the case where רבי יונתן says the הלכה follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: A neck chain or iron collar put on someone being led to execution.
A bill of divorce.
Someone setting sail on a sea voyage.
A caravan traveling to a far place.
At first, meaning the earlier ruling before it was expanded.

steps.confusionAlert: The man only said 'write' a גט, not 'give' it. The חידוש is that in these dangerous situations we also give it to her.

phrases.english: The dangerously ill case, as we learned:
At first they used to say,
one who is led out in a neck chain
phrases.notes: He is being taken out to be executed.

phrases.english: and said: 'Write a bill of divorce for my wife,'
these people should write it and give it.
They later said:
even one who sets sail and one who leaves with a caravan.
Rabbi Shimon ben Shezuri says:
even one who is dangerously ill.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסוּכָּן, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the two cases listed in step 20 by quoting its source משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רבי שמעון שזורי, a dangerously ill man who says 'write a גט for my wife' has his גט written and given. רבי יונתן says the הלכה follows him here.

steps.title: The source for the second case: תרומת מעשר of דמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in דמאי where רבי שמעון שזורי rules that if תרומת מעשר of דמאי fell back into its produce, one may ask the seller, even on a weekday, and rely on his word.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of תרומת מעשר of דמאי is what we learned in a משנה: If תרומת מעשר of דמאי fell back into its place, רבי שמעון בן שזורי says: Even on a weekday, you may ask the seller and eat based on what he says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is showing us where the second case from רבי יונתן's list, תרומת מעשר of דמאי, comes from. It quotes a משנה where רבי שמעון שזורי gives a lenient ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, רב אשי said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי only for a מסוכן and for תרומת מעשר of דמאי. Step 21 showed the source for מסוכן, and this step shows the source for תרומת מעשר of דמאי. The point is that רבי שמעון שזורי's ruling on בן פקועה is not on this list, so רב אשי does not have to follow him there.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion the לוי gives to a כהן from the מעשר he receives. It is holy, and a non-כהן may not eat it.
Produce bought from an עם הארץ, who may not have tithed properly, so it must be tithed again just in case.
That went back to its place. The separated portion fell back and got mixed into the produce it was taken from.
A regular weekday, as opposed to שבת or יום טוב.
Based on his word. You rely on what the seller tells you.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יונתן's two cases where the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי are (1) a מסוכן ordering a גט and (2) תרומת מעשר of דמאי that fell back into its produce. Since בן פקועה is not one of them, רב אשי can rule against רבי שמעון שזורי there and require שחיטה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes רב אשי's defense. רבי יונתן's tradition limits the rule 'הלכה כרבי שמעון שזורי' to just these two cases, so the objection of אדא בר חבו is answered.

phrases.english: Teruma of the tithe of demai, as we learned in a Mishnah:
Teruma of the tithe of demai
that returned to its place,
phrases.notes: He means it fell back and got mixed into the same produce it was separated from.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Shezuri says:
Even on a weekday, one asks him
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the seller of the produce.

phrases.english: and eats it based on his word.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר שֶׁל דְּמַאי, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 21. Step 21 gave the source for the first case on רבי יונתן's list (מסוכן), and this step gives the source for the second case (תרומת מעשר of דמאי).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון שזורי rules that when תרומת מעשר of דמאי falls back into its produce, one may ask the seller, even on a weekday, and eat based on his statement.
